Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front and then the attached redline: DPA_Redline_olga_v1.docx and SCCs-mapping.xlsx.

- SCCs: We propose the new EU Commission SCCs (2021 / processor module) with a processor-to-processor addendum for specific subprocessing (we include both options in the mapping).
- Model training: Our standard approach is to limit training on customer prompt-output pairs unless explicitly contracted. We have a Transfer Impact Addendum template; I've included the clause in the DPA redline (see section 5.3).
- Retention: We provide configurable retention windows. Draft options included: 60 days (default logs), 90 days (support bundle), 180 days (audit window, requires procurement approval and small surcharge).

Key asks from our side:
1) Please confirm whether Mercury requires controller-to-controller SCCs for any downstream analytics partners — that will change exhibit scoping.
2) If the customer wants persistent training (long-term model updates), we need that flagged in the order form so we can surface cost/ops notes.

Next steps: Ben (legal) / Laura (contracts) — can you review the attached DPA redline and confirm if the processor-to-processor addendum and the 180-day retention option are acceptable to legal/finance? If not, recommend alternate language by EOD tomorrow.

Olga Petrov

Olga / Laura / Anna — quick legal notes inline below and attached (Ben_comments_DPA.pdf).

On the proposed DPA: we should keep the processor module SCCs as the baseline, but explicitly include a processor-to-processor clause when subprocessing chains exist (clause 4.2 in our DPA redline). I added fallback language for temporary routing to non-EU regions if (a) we notify Mercury within 48 hours and (b) we implement equivalent safeguards and encryption in transit + at rest.

Training carveout (section 5.3): I recommend tightening the wording — change "may be used" to "will not be used for model improvements absent an executed Training Addendum". This preserves our ability to offer training as a paid option while protecting Mercury.

Retention windows: agree with offering 90-day default. 180-day reserved as a paid option with explicit SOW line item. Added a short clause requiring that long-term retention be recorded in the Order Form with a pricing line.

Escalation: if Mercury cannot accept the 90-day default + optional 180-day paid upgrade, escalate to Marissa Cole (VP Legal).
